products.title: Laba Gesha - Natural Sundried
products.body_html:
Laba Gesha is a small community on the outskirts of the famed Yirgacheffe district, bordering Ethiopia's Bule mountain range. Because of the area's high altitude and cooler climate, local farmers traditionally relied more on cereal crop production than coffee farming. As the climate has changed, more coffee is being produced here, and two years ago, our exporting partner, GBroad Trading, started working with a small group of farmers in the village. Although this town shares the name ‘Gesha’ with the famous coffee variety whose origins lie in Western Ethiopia, no Gesha trees grow here. Instead, farmers in the area cultivate Kurume, 74110 and 74112, common across the Yirgacheffe area. In the cup, we find delicate notes of strawberry cream alongside sweet pastry and cocoa.

Pronunciation: LAH-bah GAY-sha

products.title: El Conacaste – Java Variety
products.body_html:
Founded in 1996 as a reforestation project, Finca Conacaste transformed 210 hectares of former corn and cattle farmland into a more biodiverse agroforestry system. Its proximity to Montecristo National Park—part of a 460-square-mile transboundary protected cloud forest spanning El Salvador, Honduras and Guatemala—made this mission especially meaningful. For years, the farm cultivated pantry staples before planting its first coffee in 2014. Since then, it has consistently ranked among the top finishers in national quality competitions like the Cup of Excellence. This particular lot, a Java variety separation, was purchased as an exclusive offering for our subscribers for its syrupy sweetness and rich notes of brown sugar and toffee.

Pronunciation: El koh-nah-KAHS-te

products.title: Finca La Hermosa - Orange Bourbon Variety
products.body_html:
Finca La Hermosa is a long-dreamed-of farm with humble beginnings. In 2010, knowing the potential of Acatenango's volcanic soil, Claudia Abril and Max Perez began transforming an abandoned parcel with no electricity or water into a thriving business. Today, this land produces Cup of Excellence-winning coffees and boasts a small poultry farm and a quality lab as well. 

Among the fields of traditional organic coffee, there is a trial plot of over 30 rarer varieties, such as Pacamara and Orange Bourbon. Orange Bourbon is a color mutation of the classic Bourbon variety, producing orange-ripening cherries instead of the typical red. What we love about this cup is the subtle brightness of dark stone fruits like cherry and plum, rounded out by a creamy milk-chocolate sweetness.

Pronunciation: FEENG-kah lah ehr-MOH-sah

products.title: Worka Chelbessa
products.body_html:

Around 765 smallholder farmers deliver ripe cherries to Worka Chelbessa, where the coffee is washed using the traditional Ethiopian method to reveal its inherent complexity. Worka Chelbessa is the first of several washing stations owned by SNAP to transition to using solar power and just the second solar-powered washing station in the country. Enjoy this beautifully expressive coffee, with sweet melon flavors, crisp tangerine-like acidity, and a jasmine floral finish.

products.title: Finca El Puente – Anaerobic Washed

Our long-time partners, Marysabel Caballero and Moisés Herrera of Finca El Puente, have built a legacy of experimentation and innovation. Over the years, we've tasted countless lots from their farm, from rare varieties to experimental processing methods. Their latest experiment explores a practical way to coax more sweetness and fruit from an otherwise classic washed profile. For this lot, the coffee cherries were left overnight in sealed sacks to ferment before depulping, washing, and drying. The result is unmistakably Finca El Puente, but with a little more fruit character than we've come to expect. Look for notes of raspberry, plum, and chocolate.

products.title: Finca Santa Elena - Pacamara Honey
products.body_html: Pacamara originated in El Salvador through crossbreeding of the local Pacas variety with Maragogipe, a variety known for its large seeds and fruity profile. This unique hybrid is synonymous with cup quality in the country. This coffee was honey processed, meaning that after the cherry’s skin was removed the seeds were dried with their sweet, sticky mucilage still intact. This processing method plays up the fruit tones of this variety, resulting in a cup that is rooted in brown sugar sweetness, with layers of juicy, tropical fruit as it cools.

products.title: Finca Santa Elena – Pacamara Honey
products.body_html:
Pacamara originated in El Salvador by crossbreeding the local Pacas variety with Maragogipe, a cultivar known for its large seeds and bold fruit flavors. This distinctive hybrid has become synonymous with high cup quality in the country and remains a staple of Salvadoran specialty coffee. Fernando Lima of Finca Santa Elena, honey processed his Pacamara variety selection this year. Halfway between a washed and natural processed coffee, this honey processed lot maintains the variety character of Pacamara while enhancing its fruit qualities. Lively tangerine and green apple flavors are softened by a sweet creaminess that rounds out the cup.

products.title: Lucio Luque
products.body_html:
In a small village deep within the Incahuasi Valley, Lucio Luque cultivates a vibrant coffee parcel, Nuevo Progresso. This section of his farm stands out for its exclusive planting of a unique variety that has redefined the region's potential for quality. Lucio's enthusiasm for this variety caught our attention, prompting us to collaborate with the cooperative and our supply chain partners to separate this coffee from the larger blend it was originally destined for. The outcome is a coffee that captivates with fruity notes of blood orange and bubble gum underpinned by delicate florals.
 
Pronunciation: LOO-see-oh LOO-keh

products.title: Incahuasi SL9 Variety
products.body_html:
The rugged and remote Incahuasi Valley is home to some of the most unique coffees we buy in South America. When we first started exploring this area with the help of our importing partner, Red Fox Coffee Merchants, we tasted samples from a few farms that stood out for their stunning complexity. We later learned this was the result of a unique coffee variety that producers referred to simply as "Inca gesha." There was certainly a resemblance to other geshas we've tried, both in the plant's appearance and in the cup, but there were also some differences. Genetic testing later revealed that this mystery variety did not at all match gesha's genetic fingerprint, but was most closely related to SL9 — a rarely cultivated variety with origins in East Africa. Though little is know about the origins of SL9, it was studied by plant breeders in the early 20th century and is thought to have been transferred to a research site in southern Peru sometime in the 1950s.

From there, it's unclear how this variety spread to a handful of farms across the region. Its popularity is growing, and though not widely cultivated, we have seen more of this variety pop up all over Peru as word of its undeniable cup quality spreads. This lot is a blend of SL9 from two neighboring farms, managed by Lucio Luque and Eudis Orosco, near the small town of Amaybamba. We've been purchasing tiny amounts of this coffee from these producers since 2018, and we're excited to finally have enough to share with our single-origin subscribers. What stands out are flavors of ripe strawberry and a range of tropical fruits like mango and starfruit, laced with complex floral notes.

Pronunciation: een-cuh-WAH-see

products.title: Bijao
products.body_html:
Huila is a rare origin for us—most of the Colombian coffees we buy come from long-term partners in the regions of Nariño and Cauca, but this year we began exploring Huila's slightly offset harvest cycle to source fresher coffee for our 100% Colombian product: Gradient. What started as a logistical curiosity led us to Bijao, a group of small producers near the community of La Plata whose name comes from a native plant traditionally used to wrap tamales. While this coffee was originally destined for a blend, its unique profile, with confectionery layers of chocolate, mixed berries, and red grape, made us want to highlight it as an exclusive offering for our single-origin subscribers.


Pronunciation: bee-HOW

Sipping these side-by-side, you’ll experience the full spectrum of these two processing methods—from the sweet notes of clementine and honey of the washed coffee to the bright strawberry and fig notes in the natural-sundried coffee.

products.title: Hassan Assalol - Natural Sundried  **SOLD OUT**
products.body_html:
Yemen’s port of Mokha has played a vital role in the global spread of coffee, and its farms preserve a rich diversity of unique and delicious coffee varieties that are well adapted to harsh climates. Despite this history, most coffee drinkers haven't tasted Yemeni coffee. Years of war have made sourcing it very challenging. However, with the support of our Yemen-based export partner, Mokha Story, we have established a purchasing relationship with Hassan Assalol, a farmer in Eastern Haraz. We have been buying Hassan’s coffee since 2018 and have collaborated on processing experiments and even a Seeds project.

Hassan’s coffee exemplifies Yemen’s distinctive cup profile, featuring intricate fruit complexity, a unique spiced quality, and a perfumed floral finish. It feels almost unfair to choose only three words to describe this coffee, but we'll call it fruit punch, cardamom, and rose.

Pronunciation: hah-SAHN ah-sah-LOHL

products.title: Nueva Llusta - Microlot

The absolute best coffees are set aside for us, and for this subscriber-exclusive offering, we’ve combined a few of our favorites that exemplify the sweet, nuanced flavors that piqued our interest when we began working with the group in 2004. These three producers–Jorge Caceres, Luis Huayhua, and Luis’ wife, Zenovia–have been consistent microlot producers for at least a decade, and we look forward to tasting their work each year. Combining their best lots together highlights the complex sweetness we love from this region, with flavors of dark chocolate, praline, and raisin.

Pronunciation: NWEH-vah USED-tuh

products.title: Valle Inca
products.body_html:
Nestled in the southern reaches of Peru's Andean highlands is a cooperative of just over 100 coffee growers determined to thrive amid extreme conditions in a rugged landscape. Despite their small size and recent formation, the Valle Inca members are taking advantage of the region's coffee revival to showcase their dedication to cultivating excellent coffee. The fruit of their labor yields notes of sweet golden raisin and creamy nougat, thanks to its blend of Bourbon and Typica varieties.

Pronunciation: VAH-yeh EEN-kah

products.title: Fundochamba - Extended Fermentation
products.body_html:
Fundochamba is a small mountain community just outside of Quilanga in Ecuador’s Loja province. We purchase from a group of 14 growers in this area who have worked together to steadily improve quality and connect with the specialty market. This year, the group dedicated a small portion of their volume to a prolonged fermentation experiment. After pulping, this coffee was fermented in a cool, low-oxygen environment for about 72 hours. The resulting cup offers intricate fruit complexity and sweetness. We taste dark-fruit notes of concord grape and black cherry, swimming in a sweet, syrupy body.

Pronunciation: Foon-Doe-Cham-bAH

products.title: Esgar Fernandez
products.body_html:
At just 19 years old, Esgar Fernandez is the youngest member of his family to take up the family business. The Fernandez family has played a central role in showcasing the quality potential of the small community of La Higuera, and we’ve had the privilege of purchasing many lots over the years from his siblings and nearby relatives. As is customary in many farming communities, Esgar was gifted a small piece of land by his family once he became an adult. Though already planted with coffee, Esgar took over the management responsibilities of this 3.5-hectare plot, which keeps him busy year-round. With guidance from his talented family, Esgar continues their tradition of excellence with a lot that explodes with complex fruit notes of blackberry, stone fruit, and clementine. 

Pronunciation: EZ-gar fair-NAHN-dez

products.title: Fundochamba
products.body_html:
Fundochamba is a small mountain community just outside of Quilanga in Ecuador’s Loja province. Here, a group of 14 growers have partnered with Roberto Jimenez of Capamaco Trading, whose experience in post-harvest processing and quality control has helped them steadily improve quality and connect with the specialty market. Years of close collaboration—focused on agronomy, processing, and overall farm health—have led to consistent gains in both cup quality and yield across the group. We love this coffee for its dried apricot-like fruit tones layered over a cozy chocolate and toasted almond base.

Pronunciation: Foon-Doe-Cham-bAH

products.title: Santafé
products.body_html:
Tucked away in the secluded eastern reaches of Nariño, the community of Santafé quietly cultivates exceptional coffee. Toldopamba, our partner in the region, supports local growers with technical assistance and quality control, enabling them to reach their full potential. We’ve focused our sourcing here since 2016, drawn by the community's strength and the outstanding quality of their coffee. The cup is big-bodied and syrupy, with layers of cocoa and dark cherry. 

Pronunciation: Santa-Fay

products.title: Toldopamba – Special Process
products.body_html:
The subscription program–backed by guaranteed volume–allows us to invest in interesting coffee each season, giving growers room to experiment without risk. This year, Toldopamba used that opportunity to explore underwater anaerobic fermentation. Coffee cherries were first washed in a circulating water bath, then run through a unique cherry sorting machine, removing any under- or overripe fruit. The uniform cherries were pulped and fermented underwater for approximately 90 hours, then cleaned in an “ecowasher” machine and dried on raised beds for 14-20 days. The result is a coffee with enhanced fruit complexity in the cup, bringing out a candied pineapple sweetness that is balanced by juicy, blood orange–like acidity.

Pronunciation:Toll-doe-Pahm-Bah

products.title: El Buen Pastor
products.body_html:
This subscriber-exclusive lot comes to us from the Cenfrocafe cooperative, our longest-running partnership in Peru. El Buen Pastor is a small association of 10 producers tending small plots in the San Pedro community of Tabaconas. Though we’ve worked with Cenfrocafe since 2007, this is our first purchase from the Tabaconas region. It’s a fairly remote area, about four hours by car from the cooperative’s headquarters in Jaen. Over the years, we’ve tasted a few small lots from Tabaconas with notable quality. When tasting through samples sent from Cenfrocafe this season, this small lot stood out to us with confectionery notes of marzipan and cocoa, underpinned by subtle flavors of stone fruit. 

Pronunciation: el BWEHN pah-STOR

products.title: Ruronzi – Natural Sundried
products.body_html:
On land shaped by both profound loss and the deep dedication of the Rwandan coffee professionals who steward it, the Ruronzi coffee farm represents a new chapter in the country’s coffee story. Owned and managed by our exporting partner, Ikawa House, this natural sundried lot comes from their second-ever harvest and is one of the best naturals we’ve tasted from Rwanda. During harvesting, thorough attention paid to cherry ripeness and slow drying results in a clean cup and complex range of fruits–most notably, sweet concord grape and juicy strawberry. 

Pronunciation: roo-RON-zee

products.title: La Viuda
products.body_html:
Coffees from the Jaén province’s southwestern districts have historically been bulked into large commodity blends, destined for anonymity. With crucial support from Origin Coffee Lab, we started digging deeper into these areas in 2019. What we found were small coffee-producing communities in and around the remote district of Colasay, producing some of our favorite coffees in Peru. A blend of this year’s selections from those farms, La Viuda bursts with juicy notes of black cherry and white grape.

Pronunciation: la vee-OO-duh

products.title: Mabono Honey Processed
products.body_html:
High in the hills of Mount Elgon, a coffee-farming community works in near isolation, transporting each sack of coffee on foot or by bike along rugged roads. Where other exporters saw impossibility, Mountain Harvest saw potential: farmers willing to try new things and invest in their future. With support from a Counter Culture Seeds grant, they built a community-run processing station that has given rise to one of the best coffees we’ve tasted in the country, Mabono Honey. Expect notes of berry, brown sugar, and a creamy body.

Pronunciation: mah-BOH-noh

products.title: Travel Tumbler – 16 oz
products.body_html:
Designed for coffee lovers on the move, this 16oz NOMAD tumbler combines clean design with all-day performance. Its fully ceramic-coated interior delivers pure taste with a seamless, color-matched finish. Double-walled and vacuum-insulated, it keeps drinks hot or cold for up to 10 hours—no leaks, no fuss. Finished with Counter Culture branding, it’s the perfect travel companion for specialty coffee anywhere.

  • Size: 16oz 
  • Color: Terra Cotta
  • Ceramic-coated interior
  • Leak-proof lid
  • Carry handle on lid
  • Fits in your cup holder
  • BPA-free
  • Top rack dishwasher safe, handwash recommended
  • Don’t ever microwave or freeze
  • Made by Created Co., designed for specialty coffee

products.title: Finca La Hermosa
products.body_html:
Born and raised among coffee plantations, Max Pérez was acutely aware of the risks and potential within the coffee industry. Driven to “make the coffee dreams come true,” he and his wife, Claudia, founded Finca La Hermosa in 2010. Situated on the slopes of the Acatenango volcano, the coffee farm benefits from fertile volcanic soils that nurture a diverse range of coffee varieties, including the Gesha, Caturra & Catuai showcased here. This coffee exhibits flavors of apricot and kiwi balanced with milk chocolate sweetness.

Pronunciation: FEENG-kah lah ehr-moh-sah

products.title: Hugo Ruiz
products.body_html:
Hugo Ruiz’s small farm overlooks the highlands of western Guatemala near the town of Concepción Huista. Hugo is a part of the CODECH cooperative, an organization we’ve worked with closely since 2010. Each season, the cooperative tastes each farmer's delivery, setting aside the highest-scoring lots to be sold at a premium, incentivizing and rewarding quality. Hugo’s coffee is regularly one of the top-scoring coffees each season. After hundreds of cups tasted, the coop identified this coffee as one of the best of the harvest, and our sourcing team couldn’t agree more. We enjoy its confectionery quality, with cocoa and nougat flavors complementing a pear-like sweetness. 


Pronunciation: hOO-go roo-EES

products.title: Decaf Idido
products.body_html:
If you’ve followed Counter Culture over the years, there’s a good chance you’ve tasted coffee from Idido. The cooperative is our longest-running partnership in East Africa, and the quality achieved by their members continues to amaze, time and time again. We decaffeinated a portion of this year’s lot, making this exceptional coffee available to a wider audience. Morning, noon, and night, Decaf Idido sings with flavors of apricot, citrus, and brown sugar.

 Pronunciation: ee-DEE-doh

products.title: Finca El Puente SL-28 Variety
products.body_html:
SL-28 is a legend in the coffee world. First selected in the 1930s by Scott Agricultural Laboratories in Kenya, the variety quickly earned recognition for its resilience and exceptional cup quality. Though it originated from a single tree discovered in Tanzania and carries a Bourbon-like genetic background, SL-28 rose to prominence in East Africa for producing some of the most complex and memorable coffees ever grown.
Today, this iconic variety has found a new home in southern Honduras at Finca El Puente, where husband-and-wife team Marysabel Caballero and Moisés Herrera cultivate it with the same dedication and precision that make their farm world-renowned. Their SL-28 is among the finest expressions we’ve tasted outside Africa: beautifully balanced yet wonderfully complex, with green apple sweetness, mouth-watering lime, and a crisp, clean finish.

Pronunciation: FEEN-kah el PWEHN-teh S-L twenty-eight

products.title: Sanctuary
products.body_html:
Sanctuary honors Counter Culture’s legacy of environmental stewardship and co-founder Fred Houk, an avid birder and environmentalist. The line first launched in 1997 to celebrate shade-grown coffees and their role in protecting biodiversity, and this limited-release blend continues that mission. It brings together coffees from shade-dense farms in Guatemala and India that honor the vital link between coffee and nature. With notes of praline, brown sugar, and apple, Sanctuary is as delicious as it is purposeful—a tribute to Fred’s vision.

The bag design features the national birds of Guatemala and India, the Resplendent Quetzal and the Indian Peafowl, respectively.

Pronunciation: SANK-choo-air-ee

products.title: Throwback Logo Hat
products.body_html:
Top off your look with a piece of history. This '90s dad hat is a nod to our beginnings, celebrating 30 years with a refreshed version of our original logo. It has that perfectly worn-in, favorite-hat feel right from the start, combining timeless style with a touch of modern nostalgia.

This hat has all the classic details you love. The faded grey color and brushed cotton finish give it a vintage vibe, while the low-profile, six-panel design ensures a comfortable, relaxed fit. It’s the perfect accessory for sunny days, casual outings, or anytime you want to carry a piece of our story with you.

Embrace the laid-back style of three decades past. Get this limited-edition dad hat before it’s gone.

products.title: Brett's Diner Mug
products.body_html:
Some things are classics for a reason. To celebrate 30 years, we’re introducing a mug that’s close to our hearts—Brett’s diner mug. This isn't just any mug—it's our founder's favorite. He believes a great coffee mug should be sturdy, timeless, and feel good in your hands. This is that mug.

Holding a generous 11oz, this classic diner mug is designed to be your new go-to. Its thick, durable ceramic walls keep your coffee perfectly warm, while the comfortable handle makes every sip a simple pleasure. Stamped with our refreshed throwback logo, this mug is a warm nod to our three-decade journey. We hope it becomes a piece of history in your kitchen too.

  • Design: Classic 11oz diner style
  • Material: Sturdy, high-quality ceramic

Pour a cup, get comfortable, and celebrate 30 years of history with us. Grab this limited-edition piece of our story before it's gone.

products.body_html:
Celebrate 30 years in style with a t-shirt that’s as classic as our story. We’ve brought back our original logo, giving it a fresh look. This isn't just a t-shirt; it's a piece of our history, designed for those who have been with us from the start and those who are just joining in.

Crafted from soft, 100% cotton, this mid-weight tee in a versatile bone color offers all-day comfort. It has that perfect, worn-in feel right from the first wear. The fit is relaxed and timeless, making it an instant staple for your wardrobe.

  • Fit: Comfortable and classic for everyday wear

Wear a piece of our legacy. Grab this limited-edition tee and celebrate three decades with us.

products.title: Finca La Victoria – Maragogipe Variety
products.body_html:
Discovered in Brazil during the late 19th century, the Maragogipe variety has become well-known for its enormous bean size and big flavors. Though its popularity has waned, many Nicaraguan producers have kept up the tradition of cultivating this unique variety. We're excited to present this lot grown on the Lovo family’s Finca La Victoria. Every year, this lot of Maragogipe is one of the best examples of the variety we taste from Latin America. Look for flavors of plum and apple, wrapped in a syrupy body.

Pronunciation: FEEN-kah lah vik-TOR-ee-uh mah-rah-go-HEE-pay

products.title: Cold Hearted
products.body_html: Sometimes the heat of the moment calls for something cold. Cold Hearted was inspired by the hot southern days that make us crave iced coffee. The blend is bright and refreshing, reminiscent of sweet tea, with layers of cherry and cocoa nibs. No matter how you brew it, Cold Hearted delivers a crisp and invigorating cup.

products.title: Arnulfo Días – Pacamara Honey
products.body_html:
Pacamara originated in El Salvador by crossbreeding the local Pacas variety with Maragogipe, a variety known for its large seeds and fruity profile. This unique hybrid has become synonymous with cup quality throughout the country. This coffee was honey processed, meaning that after the coffee cherry’s skin was removed, the seeds were dried with their sweet, sticky mucilage intact. This processing method plays up the fruit tones of this variety, resulting in a syrupy sweet cup with notes of brown sugar and red grape.

 
Pronunciation: Are-NOOL-foh DEE-ahs

products.title: Cold Coffee Bundle
products.body_html:
With bright citrus notes and a delicate floral finish, our year-round favorite, Apollo, truly shines over ice. Featuring organic, washed coffee from Ethiopia! This special two-pack gives you double the coffee, perfect for crushable iced brews.

Looking for an Iced Coffee recipe to get started? We recommend:

  • 30g of fresh-roasted, whole-bean coffee
  • 335g of filtered water at 200°F
  • 165g of ice
  • Your favorite pour-over brewer

Don’t miss this limited-time bundle—it’s only here for the season!

products.title: Finca La Hermosa - Pink Bourbon Variety
products.body_html:
Born and raised among coffee plantations, Max Pérez understood both the risks and potential of the coffee industry long before starting a farm. Driven to “make their coffee dreams come true,” he and his wife, Claudia, founded Finca La Hermosa in 2010. Situated on the slopes of the Acatenango volcano, the coffee farm benefits from fertile soils that nurture a diverse range of coffee varieties. This lot is a separation of their Pink Bourbon, exhibiting bright red plum flavors balanced by milk chocolate sweetness.

Pronunciation: FEENG-kah lah ehr-MOH-sah

products.title: Sipi - Natural Sundried
products.body_html:
At the forefront of Uganda’s specialty coffee movement, our partners at Kawacom are redefining expectations for the country’s coffee. While Uganda is best known for commercial-grade robusta, Kawacom works with high-elevation arabica grown in the fertile soils of Mount Elgon and processes it with extraordinary care. Their naturally sundried coffees showcase what’s possible when quality and consistency guide every step. Look for notes of Concord grape and chocolate, with a juicy body.

Pronunciation: SIP-ee NATCH-ur-uhl

products.title: La Golondrina – Honey Processed
products.body_html:
La Golondrina is a coffee we return to year after year. This lot offers something new.

Since 2007, we've partnered with the Orgánica cooperative in Cauca, Colombia, whose members share our dedication to quality and sustainability. Their flagship coffee, La Golondrina, has become one of our most beloved single origins.

For this special release, several cooperative members experimented with honey processing. By removing the skin of ripe coffee cherries but leaving the sticky fruit mucilage intact during drying, they created coffee with a distinctly different character.

This lot offers a lively twist on the familiar La Golondrina profile, with expressive fruit flavors and notes of raspberry and lime.

Pronunciation: Lah go-lun-DREE-nuh HUN-ee

products.title: Urcunina - Anaerobic Honey
products.body_html:
Urcunina is the name indigenous Quillasingas people call the Galeras volcano, a striking landmark in La Florida, Nariño. When the Asprocaes farmers association was established through the Borderlands project, members chose this name for their coffee as a way to set it apart from others in the region. Since then, they’ve continued to distinguish their offerings by exploring innovative processing methods. Their latest creation is this anaerobic honey processed coffee, which has a sweet syrupy body and deep fruit tones of plum and red grape. 

Pronunciation: oor-koo-NEE-na

Origin photo images credit to Jorge E. Moncayo Torres

products.title: Borderlands Microlot
products.body_html:
Last week’s single origin subscription featured a coffee from the Borderlands project—an initiative that united coffee producers in Nariño, Colombia, to enhance their livelihoods and build enduring relationships with quality-driven buyers. Over time, these groups have invested in variety-specific plots to better understand how high-quality cultivars perform in their unique soil and climate. 

This subscriber-exclusive microlot is sourced from plots growing SL-28 and Gesha––two prized African varieties. Grown in the Colombian Andes, they offer a unique tasting experience: the bright citrus and floral quality of these varieties are beautifully complemented by the sweet chocolate and stone fruit characteristics that define Nariño’s typical cup.

products.title: Field Trip
products.body_html:
This limited-release blend honors the people and places behind our favorite beverage and highlights the craft and care that create exceptional coffee experiences.

Sourced seasonally from farms in the southern hemisphere, Field Trip blends bright coffees to create a crisp, vibrant cup. Expect sweet notes of blackberry and clementine.

products.title: Birthday Blend
products.body_html: Birthday Blend is a celebration of Counter Culture’s 31 years in specialty coffee. This fruit-forward coffee offers layers of flavors with a creamy, balanced body. Crafted to honor our legacy of quality and creativity, it’s a toast to the past, present, and future of exceptional coffee. Great coffee, like a great celebration, should be unforgettable. Cheers to more than three decades of deliciousness.

products.title: Eudis Orosco - Gesha Variety
products.body_html:
Eudis Orosco named his farm Finca Villa Vista—an apt name for a farm that sits at a staggering 2,117 meter altitude with stunning views of snow-capped mountains and lush plant life. Eudis originally learned farm management from his father and refined his practices over the years with help from his cooperative, Incahuasi. From a section of his farm dedicated to the cultivation of the Gesha variety, this is an exquisite example of how amazing geography, coffee variety, and quality control produce a first-rate coffee with notes of blackberry, floral, and tropical fruit.  

Pronunciation: "Eh-oo-dees Oh-rohs-ko

products.title: Orgánica Microlot
products.body_html:
This coffee represents the continued evolution of a partnership we’ve maintained for nearly 2 decades. Growers in the Orgánica cooperative have focused on achieving the highest quality in every aspect of their production, including planting higher-quality, harder-to-grow varieties. This lot features their Pink Bourbon and Gesha selections. While the cup may not present the overt florals often associated with these varieties’ Ethiopian lineage, it offers a compelling expression of Colombia’s evolving coffee culture. Expect sweet flavors of raspberry and honey, balanced by a tea-like body.

Pronunciation: Ore-GANN-ee-cah Microlot

products.title: Borderlands
products.body_html: In 2012, Catholic Relief Services launched the Borderlands project to connect coffee growers in Nariño, Colombia, with the specialty market, offering farmers divided by conflict a new path to prosperity by working as a community. This collaboration unlocked the region’s coffee quality potential and created lasting economic opportunities. The culmination of these efforts is in the cup: Sweet milk chocolate and almond flavors are balanced with a crisp citrus acidity and a nectarine-like finish.

products.title: Burera
products.body_html:
The Burera district in Rwanda is known for its rich volcanic soils that support abundant fruit and vegetable farming. Historically, coffee has not been grown here, but a new project is underway to change that. Farmers are planting coffee trees all across the district, creating an important source of income diversification. The early results are impressive, with excellent quality emerging from the region. We find black currant and a range of juicy tropical fruits in our cups. 
 
Pronunciation: boo-RARE-ra

Images courtesy of M.O Studios and Ikawa House

products.title: Yonal Fernandez
products.body_html:
The coffees we source from the Colasay region have quickly become some of our favorites in all of Peru. Yonal Fernandez is part of a small group of producers in Colasay whose coffee we began purchasing in late 2019. His coffee has been featured in  Fast Forward and La Viuda, but this is the first time we’re showcasing it as a unique microlot. 
Together with his wife, Imelda, Yonal cultivates the unique Bourbon de Colasay variety–a regional mutation that performs equally well in the field and in the cup. We’ve had the opportunity to spend time with Yonal during our visits over the years, sharing meals and learning about what makes this region so special. Colasay’s combination of rugged terrain, unique varieties, and highly skilled producers are a recipe for exceptional quality. We’re excited to highlight Yonal’s work with this small lot, available only to our single origin subscribers. Look for sweet and balanced notes of raisin, chocolate, and brown sugar that epitomize the excellence emerging from Colasay.

Pronunciation: yo-NAL fer-NAN-dez

products.title: La Palestina - Marshell Variety
products.body_html:
La Palestina began as a small plot planted by Don Juan Alarcón in 1978. As his family grew, so did the size of the farm as he purchased additional land to pass on to his children. Over time, the Alarcóns have worked to create a farm that seamlessly weaves together tradition and innovation. Since our first visit to Palestina in 2018, we’ve seen a range of investments that have not only improved coffee quality but also increased biodiversity. This exclusive lot comes to us from the plot of Juan’s son, Jose Praxedes Alarcón. It’s a single variety called Marshell–a local mutation related to Catimors but with a cup quality that sets it apart. We taste sweet and fruity notes of fig and cola, bolstered by a crisp finish. 


Pronunciation: la pal-ess-TEEN-uh mar-SHELL

products.title: Intango
products.body_html:
Intango traces its roots back to a USAID-funded initiative that transformed Rwanda’s coffee industry. The PEARL project invested at every stage of production, laying the foundation for Rwanda’s specialty coffee sector. Counter Culture engaged early, mentoring local professionals, including Gilbert Gatali, who later purchased one of the first PEARL-constructed washing stations and founded Intango. Gilbert believes in coffee's potential to transform lives, and his passion for coffee and the people behind it is inspiring to witness. We taste notes of apricot, citrus, and black tea—a classic Rwanda profile that keeps us coming back year after year. 

Pronunciation: in-TAHN-go

products.title: Fast Forward
products.body_html: Enjoying fresh, delicious coffee should be a year-round affair. That's why Fast Forward is a curated blend of similar coffees from different harvest periods, ensuring you can savor the freshest flavors no matter the season. The ever-changing selection of organic coffees guarantees a delightful balance of nutty and sweet notes, wrapped in a creamy body that will leave you craving another cup.

products.title: Finca La Hermosa Gesha – Dual Process
products.body_html:
Born and raised among coffee plantations, Max Pérez was acutely aware of both the risks and potential within the coffee industry. Driven by a desire to “make the coffee dreams come true,” he and his wife, Claudia, founded Finca La Hermosa in 2010. Situated on the slopes of the Acatenango volcano, the coffee farm benefits from fertile volcanic soils that nurture a diverse range of coffee varieties, including an entire “Gesha forest.” This coffee combines two distinct processing techniques - honey and natural sundried. The honey process incorporates anaerobic fermentation while leaving the sticky mucilage on the coffee seed for 2 days before being dried. Through the natural process, coffee cherries are dried with their fruit intact for 30 days on raised beds. Roasting these two coffees together results in the distinguished characteristics of blueberry, honeysuckle and limeade, a beautiful reflection of both processes and variety.

Pronunciation: FEENG-kah lah ehr-moh-sah

products.title: El Batan
products.body_html:
El Batan is a small coffee-farming community nestled in the highlands of Loja, Ecuador. This year, four farms from the area approached Roberto Jiménez, our export partner in Ecuador, seeking his help to connect with a buyer for their coffee. When Roberto shared a sample with us, we were immediately impressed by the quality and knew it would be a perfect fit for our Single Origin Subscription program. Each grower carefully harvested and pulped uniformly ripe red coffee cherries, then fermented the coffee for 48 hours––about a day longer than is typical––to enhance fruit flavors in the cup. Look for jammy plum and blackberry flavors rooted in a deep chocolatey sweetness.

Pronunciation: El ba-TAHN

products.body_html:
Searching for the perfect gift to thrill the coffee connoisseur in your life? A Counter Culture Gift Digital Card is the ultimate way to deliver the joy of freshly roasted coffee while giving them the freedom to choose their favorites. With the option to include a personalized message and schedule the delivery for the perfect moment, it's more than a gift—it's an invitation to elevate their coffee experience!

products.title: Dambi Udo – Natural Sundried
products.body_html: Before coffee became a global commodity, it was produced like Dambi Udo Natural Sundried: cultivated in Ethiopia's forests under a dense canopy of shade, harvested by hand, and dried as whole cherries. At the Guji Highland estate in Dambi Udo village, they preserve this tradition while using modern techniques to harness the complex flavors of coffee's origin. Sun drying on raised beds imparts vibrant, saturated fruit flavors in the cup reminiscent of ripe blueberries, dried dates, and cocoa.

products.title: Best In Snow Bundle
products.body_html:
Our Bestseller bundle brings together two of our most beloved coffees. Year after year, Big Trouble and La Golondrina take the top spots for our best-selling year-round blend and best-selling single-origin coffees. Try the classic rich and nutty profiles of Big Trouble and La Golondrina and see why they are favorites among coffee enthusiasts.

  • Best-Sellers: Big Trouble and La Golondrina are best-selling coffees in their categories, celebrated for their exceptional flavors.
  • Nutty Notes: Both blends feature delightful nutty undertones, creating a cohesive tasting experience.
  • Versatile Brewing: Whether enjoyed as an espresso, pour-over, or drip, these coffees cater to every brewing preference.
  • Bundle and save: Save 25% and explore these fan favorites.

products.title: Kanelite Estate
products.body_html: Kanelite Estate is run by the wife and husband team Irene Njagi and Nelson Muchiri. This second generation farm is located in Embu near Mt. Kenya's eastern slopes, in some of the best coffee growing conditions in the country. Focused on quality processing and community building, the estate measures success both in cup quality and the well-being of the people who work there. This year's harvest is sweet and savory, with notes of black currant, tamarind and sungold tomato.

products.body_html:
