products.title: Kamwea Estate
products.body_html: For Nyaga Kamwea, the Kamwea Estate is both a tribute to his late father and a legacy he hopes to pass on to his son. Located in Kenya's eastern province, an area known more for corn than coffee, the Kamwea estate defies this reputation by producing some of the highest-quality coffee in the area. This year’s harvest boasts bright citrus balanced by currant and nectarine fruit tones.

products.title: Muriama Estate
products.body_html:
Muriama estate is a reimagined second-generation coffee farm in Kenya that reflects a family’s commitment to progress. Founded in 1954 with just 100 trees, the family spent decades selling coffee cherries to the local “coffee factory,” where they were processed and blended with coffee from other growers. Through incremental investments, they gained more control over how their coffee tastes and where it’s sold. Years of quality improvement have culminated in the bold, yet delicate flavors in the cup: bright grapefruit acidity balanced by black currant compote sweetness and a silky mouthfeel. 


Pronunciation: Moo-ree-AH-mah

products.title: Gigantic
products.body_html: Coffee beans come in all shapes and sizes. Gigantic is a blend of Pacamara—a variety of the Arabica coffee plant that produces exceptionally large beans. The combination results in a complex coffee with big big notes of fuji apple, nectarine, and caramel.

products.title: CaféNor Pacamara
products.body_html: Pacamara, a remarkable coffee variety from El Salvador, is the result of crossbreeding the local Pacas variety with Maragogipe, a variety known for its large bean size and outsized, punchy flavor. This unique hybrid is a hallmark of Salvadorian specialty coffee, and our partners at Cafenor have curated a stunning example of the variety's full potential. This coffee is a blend of both washed and honey-processed coffee and is brimming with vibrant fruit flavors. Look for notes of juicy stone fruit and red grapes rooted in deep chocolatey sweetness.

products.title: Bulk Coffee
products.body_html: Upgrade your coffee routine with our bulk bags, made for true coffee lovers. Each bag brews 48 to 160 cups of our signature blends, perfect for keeping your favorites on hand. Save and sip through the holiday season!

products.title: Duromina
products.body_html:
The Duromina Cooperative emerged from a Technoserve project that transformed coffee production in Agaro, Ethiopia. Before the project, coffee in this area was considered low-quality and sold at low prices. Quality training, infrastructure investments, and cooperative business administration have resulted in high-quality coffee and economic opportunities for farmers. Duromina’s success is reflected in its beautifully expressive coffee: sweet, tea-like, and perfumed with honeysuckle-like florals and stone fruit flavors.

Pronunciation: doo-roh-MEE-nah

products.title: Polar Espresso Bundle
products.body_html:
Elevate your espresso with our two fan-favorite coffees for espresso. With low acidity and a medium-dark roast level, Big Trouble’s caramel, nutty, and round notes make it perfect for espresso. Forty-Six offers a more classic and traditional espresso experience - it’s dark, rich, and flavorful. Both roasted to perfection, these coffees shine as espresso and pair perfectly with milk for lattes or cappuccinos.

  • Perfect espresso harmony: Both Big Trouble and Forty-Six deliver flavors ideal for espresso. Enjoy these coffees with milk for lattes or cappuccinos, unlocking a new dimension of flavor.
  • Espresso and more: While both of these coffees shine brewed as espresso, you can use any brewing method you want! Try them as a pour-over or French press and experience their range.
  • Bundle and save: Save 20% and explore these go-to espresso coffee blends.

products.title: Dark Roast Bundle
products.body_html:
Featuring our two darkest roasted coffees, Gradient and Forty-Six, this set is perfect for those who appreciate the bold and indulgent notes of dark roasts. Even with a darker roast, these high-quality coffees maintain complex, delicious, and unique. Don’t miss out on trying the darkest and richest roasts in the Counter Culture Coffee line-up.

  • Dark and delicious: Gradient and Forty-Six offer a rich and indulgent experience, perfect for dark roast enthusiasts.
  • Versatile Brewing: Whether enjoyed as an espresso or pour-over these coffees cater to every brewing preference.
  • Bundle and save: Save 20% and explore the darkest Counter Culture Coffee blends.

products.title: Pompilio Garcia Luna
products.body_html:
Just outside the remote community of San Vicente Yogondoy, Pompilio Garcia Luna tends to a plot of traditional coffee varieties that have helped define the legacy of southern Oaxacan coffees for generations. Nestled in the lush shade canopy of the Sierra Sur mountain range, his farm is home to Pluma Hidalgo—an adaptation of the Typica varieties that were amongst the first coffee trees brought to the Americas—as well as Bourbon and Caturra trees. Pompilio’s meticulous cherry selection and processing results in a prime example of a top-quality Oaxacan coffee. We taste notes of dark chocolate and dried fruit tied together with a panela-like sweetness.

Pronunciation: pom-PEEL-ee-o gar-SEE-ah LOO-nuh

products.title: Jabanto – Natural Sundried
products.body_html:
Counter Culture’s relationship with the Jabanto farmers group is the epitome of transparent and traceable sourcing in Ethiopia. Its members have worked hard to build an enterprising business from scratch, and their commitment to careful harvesting and processing each year results in some of our favorite offerings. Jabanto Natural Sundried showcases a range of flavors that have made naturally processed coffee from Yirgacheffe so famous. We taste fruit notes of blueberry alongside delicate florals and sweet pastry.
 
Pronunciation: jah-BAHN-toh

products.title: Shiferaw Dukale - Natural Sundried
products.body_html:
Counter Culture has partnered with the Jabanto farmers' group since its formation in 2017. Most of the coffee they produce is natural sundried, and each year we have the privilege of tasting a wide range of exceptional single-farmer lots. Even amongst this impressive lineup, Shiferaw Dukale’s coffee stood out for its unique fruit complexity and sweetness. We taste classic notes of blueberry mingling alongside pecan and cocoa.
 
Pronunciation: shih-feh-RAWH doo-KEH-leh

products.title: Equilibrium
products.body_html:
Equilibrium is comprised of three unique coffees. In this equal-parts blend, each component melds with one another to create a new flavor experience. Our Coffee team tastes notes of stone fruit & tangerine, and considers this one of our most dynamic offerings of the year! 

Pronunciation: ee-kwa-LIB-bree-um

products.title: Gemini
products.body_html: When the opportunity arose to create our first collaborative product with another roaster, we looked to the global stage. We’ve partnered with Fritz Coffee of Korea, whose dedication to quality and craftsmanship mirrors our own. By exchanging green (unroasted) coffee from some of our best suppliers, we crafted a product that reaches new horizons and celebrates our shared commitment to excellence. This coffee pairing bursts with juicy notes of apple and blueberry complemented by soft melon flavors.

products.title: Mountain Harvest Peaberry
products.body_html: This coffee comes to us via Mountain Harvest, a company working to improve the quality of Ugandan coffee while making the communities that grow it more sustainable. This coffee is a special peaberry selection from farms on Mount Elgon. Peaberries occur when one seed develops inside a coffee fruit instead of two. Sorting them out is extra work, but it’s worth it for their dynamic and sweet flavors. We taste apricot, black tea, and coconut.

products.title: Mountain Harvest
products.body_html:
Mountain Harvest is a beacon of change in Uganda's coffee sector, championing quality, sustainability, and equity for farmers. Since partnering in 2018, we've witnessed the remarkable evolution of their impact initiatives, resulting in coffees we love drinking and progress we're proud to support. This year’s offering, a blend from farms on Mount Elgon, sings with notes of citrus, ginger, and molasses.

Pronunciation: MOWN-tin HAAR-vist

Photo credits: Mountain Harvest, Jjumba Martin

products.title: Luis Huayhua
products.body_html:
Luis Huayhua of Nueva Llusta, Bolivia, continues to be an exemplary farmer—producing some of the best coffee in the CENAPROC cooperative. Dedicated to educating and encouraging his fellow farmers to pursue better picking and processing techniques, he’s a natural leader. This year's harvest is juicy with tropical fruit and cherry flavors.

Pronunciation: loo-WEES WY-wuh

products.title: Pedro Patana
products.body_html: Pedro Patana’s commitment to developing a coffee community in the depths of Bolivia’s tropical Yungas region is only surpassed by his drive to provide for his wife and family. Out of necessity and hardship, Pedro and his wife put down roots in a largely uninhabited area where they’d be the first to plant coffee alongside other essential crops. As the founder of CENAPROC, a cooperative established in 1992, Pedro still strives to improve coffee production among his neighbors, focusing on quality, organic practices and shared access to resources. Pedro’s hard work shines through in this year’s coffee harvest where we experience the sweet taste of dried cherry and milk chocolate.

products.title: K’uychi
products.body_html:
Since 2015, we’ve purchased coffee from producers nestled deep in the mountains of Nariño, Colombia. The area has a history of heavy guerrilla activity that, for decades, isolated the community and discouraged collective business efforts. Against all odds, the producers of K’uychi have worked together to improve their farms, conserve their community’s natural resources, and bring us this wonderful coffee. We taste notes of green grape, clementine, and milk chocolate.


Pronunciation: koo-EE-chee

products.title: Even Keel Half-Caff
products.body_html: Find your balance with every sip. Even Keel’s carefully crafted blend of caffeinated and decaffeinated organic coffees ensures you stay on course. With notes of graham cracker and molasses, Even Keel is a smooth and satisfying coffee that’s perfect all day long.

products.title: Finca Virgen de Copacabana
products.body_html: Amid the dense, tropical Yungas rainforest and poised between two rivers, Finca Virgen de Copacabana perseveres through a notoriously difficult place to produce and export high-quality coffee. Neighboring the ecological preserve and park at Alto Beni, this coffee farm coexists with some of Bolivia’s most lush and remote biosphere. For more than 20 years owner Maria Nidia continues to pursue quality and sustainability by investing in new coffee varieties and processing equipment as well as inspiring the next generation of young coffee professionals. Look for notes of milk chocolate, raisin and nougat.<br data-mce-fragment="1">

products.title: Silent Night Bundle (Decaf)
products.body_html:
This bundle is curated specifically for those who savor the rich warmth of coffee without the buzz. Featuring our cult-classic decaf Slow Motion and a rotating single-origin decaf, we promise an amazing coffee experience that doesn’t compromise on flavor. Unwind, sip, and embrace the flavor of high-quality coffee with every cup.

  • Premium decaffeinated beans: We meticulously source coffees for decaffeination, ensuring the coffee’s inherent flavors come through.
  • Versatile brewing: Whether you prefer a French press, pour-over, or drip, these decaf blends are perfect for any brewing method.
  • Bundle and save: Save 20% and try these coffees that are just as delicious as their caffeinated counterparts.

products.title: Nelson Melo
products.body_html: Nelson Melo and his wife, Liliana Pabón, are the visionaries behind Orgánica. At Finca Las Acacias, they set the standard for our exceptional La Golondrina coffee. While neighboring farms chose robust varieties during renovations, Nelson and Liliana took a different path, opting for high-quality but more demanding varieties. Their commitment to organic methods and meticulous processing results in a coffee that stands out for its nuanced flavors, boasting notes of bergamot, kiwi, and sweet apple pastry.

products.title: Finca El Puente - Gesha Variety
products.body_html:
Our relationship with Finca El Puente, which has spanned two decades, is rooted in a shared commitment to quality and a belief that remarkable coffees should be accessible to more people.

This year, we sourced a small amount of their Gesha, an iconic variety that Moisés and Marysabel were the first to cultivate in Honduras. Thanks to their partnership and dedication, we can share it at an accessible price, giving the wider coffee community a taste of their vision and what makes Finca El Puente so special. Look for floral aromatics, crisp green apple brightness, and a smooth chocolate sweetness in the cup.

products.title: Valle Del Santuario
products.body_html:
In 2007, Counter Culture embarked on a new, more transparent model of sourcing in northern Peru. We focused on coffee from five communities in the high-elevation areas of Ihuamaca, just outside of San Ignacio. Our relationships in this region are some of our longest-standing with producers anywhere in the world. Through many changes in this region since those early days, producers’ dedication to quality and environmental stewardship has remained steady. Sweet and approachable, look for balanced notes of toffee, vanilla and dried fruit.

Pronunciation: VIE-yay del san-TWAR-ee-o

products.title: Intango – Dark Roast
products.body_html:
The Intango coffee washing station is owned by Gilbert Gatali, a widely recognized leader in Rwanda’s relatively young and thriving specialty coffee sector. Gilbert believes in coffee's potential to transform lives and his passion for coffee and the people behind it are inspiring to witness. This year, we’re excited to explore how a darker roasting style offers new dimensions to the delicate and fruity flavors often found in Rwandan coffees. At this roast level, we first notice a full and velvety body complemented by sweet flavors of dark chocolate and dried fig.

Pronunciation: in-TAHN-go

products.title: Alto Ihuamaca
products.body_html:
Alto Ihuamaca is one of the five coffee-producing communities which makes up Valle del Santuario, one of our most tenured single origin products. During our selection process for Valle del Santuario, we often taste coffees separated by specific communities or farms. This year, a small lot from five producers in Alto Ihuamaca caught our attention, evoking memories of the flavors that initially sparked our interest in this remote area way back in 2007. We reserved this special lot exclusively for our subscribers, some of whom have been exploring coffees from this region with us since the beginning. This is a deeply sweet coffee highlighted by notes of milk chocolate and caramel with a crisp acidity reminiscent of green grapes.

Pronunciation: AL-toh  e-wuh-MAH-ka

products.title: Eladio Chamba - Anaerobic Washed
products.body_html:
Through curiosity and a willingness to try something new, Eladio Chamba transformed his family’s pig farm into one of the best coffee farms in Ecuador. Eladio’s coffee has been recognized in local and national quality competitions and has been a mainstay on our menu since 2016. For the past few seasons, he has experimented with anaerobic fermentation in his post-harvest processing, resulting in stunningly complex coffee. The year's harvest offers bright, juicy stone fruit and white grape flavors, imbued with a soft floral sweetness.

Pronunciation: eh-LAH-dyoh CHAHM-bah

products.title: 12oz Year-Round Blends
products.body_html:
Discover Counter Culture Coffee’s Year-Round Blends: 
Explore a curated selection of blends featuring diverse origins, flavor profiles, organic options, and decaf varieties—crafted for every coffee lover, every day of the year.

products.title: Yacuri
products.body_html: Comprised of 431 square kilometers of protected forest, Yacuri National Park straddles the border of southern Ecuador’s Loja and Zamora-Chinchipe provinces. For generations, farmers in the periphery of the park have managed organic agroforestry systems, protecting the land for future generations and preserving the area's stunning biodiversity. In 2023, Caravela Coffee—one of our export partners— helped a group of these growers obtain organic certification, to reward their sustainable practices with organic premiums. The coffee here is sweet like brown sugar, with round, buttery, almond tones that give way to a dried apricot finish.

products.title: Urcunina – Extended Fermentation
products.body_html:
For the first time since our partnership began in 2012, the ASPROCAES association ran a series of small processing trials this season, extending their coffee’s fermentation time to measure its impact on quality. This lot fermented for 36 hours—nearly triple the typical duration—in a low-oxygen environment. Special effort was made to ensure this fermentation took place under cool conditions to avoid the boozy, sour flavors of over-fermentation. The resulting cup has intense stone fruit qualities and a crisp green apple brightness. We admire the group’s commitment to quality enhancement and are excited to share this experimental coffee with you.

Pronunciation: oor-koo-NEE-na

products.title: Buliza
products.body_html:
The coffees produced at the Buliza washing station are the result of an innovative collaboration between a cooperatively owned union and private exporter. Just an hour north of the bustling capital of Kigali, producers from UCOCARU cooperative union deliver their fresh coffee cherries for processing under the care of the washing station’s experienced quality team. The results showcase a classic Rwandan flavor profile of red fruits running the gamut from fresh cranberry to dried fruit leather tied together with a delightfully crisp and clean body.

Pronunciation: boo-LEE-zuh

products.title: Kushikamana
products.body_html:
Kushikamana blossomed from a partnership between Counter Culture and a group of small-estate farmers near Mt. Kenya. The vision was to establish a more direct and transparent purchase model than Kenya’s typical export routes allow. These autonomous growers named the alliance Kushikamana, Swahili for "connected.” This selection embodies the iconic Kenyan coffee profile, delivering the perfect balance of sweet and savory, with notes of dried fruit and bright, crisp citrus.

Pronunciation: koo-shee-kah-MAH-nah

products.title: Ngarutua
products.body_html:
The Muthathai family, owners of Ngarutua Estate, have been growing coffee on the slopes of Mount Kenya since 1958. Today, Peterson and Purity Muthathai run the farm with the help of their children. Over the years, they have focused on retaining more value from the coffee production on their farm by investing in processing infrastructure and coordinating efforts with nearby small estates to improve quality and market access. Years of quality innovations have culminated in this big bodied coffee that has bright grapefruit acidity balanced by sweet, juicy blackberry flavors. 

Pronunciation: eN-Gar-OO-too-uh

products.title: ASUVIM
products.body_html:
Nestled in the mountains overlooking beautiful Lake Atitlán in southwestern Guatemala, ASUVIM is a small coffee association with a unified focus on quality. Each evening, approximately 65 producers in the area bring their ripe coffee cherries to a central mill where this lot is processed. The result is an exceptionally clean and vibrant coffee that showcases the best of this region’s coffee flavors. Enjoy notes of stone fruit and milk chocolate, accompanied by a syrupy body. 

Pronunciation: ah-soo-VEEM

products.title: Iridescent
products.body_html:
Iridescent’s sweet notes of chocolate, blueberries, and marmalade evoke memories of cozy winter mornings and holiday traditions. With $1 per pound funding transformative sustainability projects in coffee-producing countries, Iridescent embodies the spirit of giving. 

Whether you're gathered around the fireplace, relishing moments with loved ones, or wrapping presents for the holidays, this blend is the perfect companion.

products.title: Guchienda
products.body_html:
Coffee is a family tradition at Guchienda estate. Esther Wanjiku Kamau and her sons, Edwin and Benson Mati, have turned this third-generation farm into an award-winning producer of exceptional coffee. This lot is sweet and bright with notes of blackberry and nectarine—reminiscent of summer’s ripest fruits.

Pronunciation: goo-chee-EN-dah

products.title: Okoluu – Natural Sundried
products.body_html:
As ripe coffee cherries dry slowly in the sun and breeze, their fruit and floral complexities deepen, enriching each coffee seed. This exceptional natural-sundried coffee comes from a group of small farms in the village of Okoluu. Sookoo Coffee, a family-owned coffee business, works closely with these growers, to implement meticulous sorting and drying protocols that achieve stunning coffee. Okoluu shines with bright blood orange like acidity, balanced by juicy strawberry sweetness and an intricate wildflower finish.

Pronunciation: oh-KOH-loo

products.title: Finca Nueva Armenia
products.body_html:
Finca Nueva Armenia is the epitome of a picturesque, bird-friendly, and biodiverse farm. We’ve worked with the owners––twin brothers Jorge and Javier Recinos––for more than 15 years, making this partnership one of our longest. This year, we isolated several top-tier lots from Finca Nueva Armenia, including a Kenyan variety called SL28. We’re delighted to offer this contemporary twist on a Counter Culture classic exclusively to our subscribers. Expect a cup brimming with the milk chocolate and apple sweetness typical of Guatemalan coffee, complemented by a creamy mouthfeel. 

Pronunciation: FEEN-kah NWAY-vah ahr-MEE-nee-ah

products.title: Sipacapa
products.body_html:
Sipacapa is more than a delicious coffee; it's a commitment to sustainability. Since its inception in 2009, the Asociación de Caficultores y Agricultores de Sipacapa (ACAS) has championed coffee production as a green alternative to the mining industry in San Marcos. The organization also supports its members’ transition to organic production. With notes of apple, simple syrup, and a lingering aftertaste of sweet cocoa, Sipacapa coffee invites you to savor the fruits of their transformation.

Pronunciation: see-pah-KAH-pah

products.title: Muthonjo
products.body_html:
The exceptional quality achieved at the Muthonjo Estate is the culmination of a whole family’s efforts throughout the year. Good farm management coupled with thoughtful picking and expert processing result in one of the best Kenyan coffees we’ve tasted this season. Look for syrupy sweet fig and blackberry tones balanced by bright grapefruit-like citrus and a delicate floral finish.

Pronunciation: moo-THON-jo

products.title: Cinco de Junio
products.body_html:
Located in the department of Madriz, the Cinco de Junio cooperative is our oldest partner in Nicaragua, a relationship that began in 2009. Over the years, the cooperative has weathered challenges–shifting economic and political conditions and the growing impacts of climate change. These pressures have forced the cooperative and its members to adjust their production practices, persevering to make the best coffee possible. This season’s lot delivers classic flavors of apple, dark chocolate, and sweet almond.
 
Pronunciation: SEEN-koh deh HOO-nyoh

products.title: Finca Nuguo - Gesha Variety 4oz Tin
products.body_html:
This coffee is the result of an extraordinary journey. Our first taste of Finca Nuguo, in 2014, didn’t shine, but it carried the spark of potential. Fast forward to today, and the Gallardo family has transformed Finca Nuguo into an absolute sensation. With feedback from Counter Culture and fellow coffee professionals, they've crafted a coffee that has taken top honors in tasting and barista competitions around the world. Year after year, Finca Nuguo is simply the best coffee we offer. This lot showcases exotic and vibrant flavors of blue raspberry candy and blood orange alongside aromatics reminiscent of magnolia blossoms. 
 
Pronunciation: FEEN-kah new-GOO-oh

products.title: Finca La Victoria – Java Variety
products.body_html:
The story of the Java variety in Latin America is deeply rooted in Nicaragua. So much so that it’s often called ‘Javanica’ throughout the region. At Finca La Victoria, owners Mario and Nelly Lovo embody a spirit of constant improvement, with experimentation at the heart of their approach. When we learned that Java was among their newest plantings, we couldn’t wait to taste the results. This small lot was worth the wait, showcasing delicate flavors of nectarine and citrus atop a tea-like body. 

Pronunciation: FEEN-kah lah vik-TOR-ee-uh JAH-vah

products.title: San Miguel
products.body_html:
In a region historically marred by mining, the Asociación de Caficultores Miguelenses (ACMI) in San Miguel Ixtahuacán offers a meaningful economic and environmental alternative. This farmer-run organization has helped its more than 450 members transition to organic practices through agronomy support, and has built the infrastructure needed to bring their coffees to the specialty market. In doing so, ACMI has helped cultivate a local economy around organic farming. Coffees from this area are nuanced yet approachable, with a sweetness reminiscent of milk chocolate and toasted almonds.

Pronunciation: sahn mee-GHEL

products.title: Sharbo Maro
products.body_html:
Purchasing coffee from a single farmer in Ethiopia is not unprecedented, but it remains relatively rare. Sharbo Maro is a member of Jabanto, a group formed in 2017 to make use of Ethiopia’s policy allowing smallholder farmers to independently export and sell their own coffees. Sharbo is one of a few Jabanto members with the infrastructure to wash coffee, making this offering all the more uncommon. The process accentuates sweet flavors of black tea, delicate floral notes, and a sparkling acidity reminiscent of limeade. 
 
Pronunciation: SHAR-boh MAR-oh

products.title: Rio de Abejas
products.body_html:
Our favorite coffees are often produced in the most stunning of settings, and the highlands of southern Oaxaca are no exception. Producers from this area have largely decided to keep their small plots planted with traditional varieties that were among the first coffee plants brought to the Americas. Well-adapted to this climate, these varieties have long contributed to Oaxacan coffee’s renowned elegance and sweetness. Look for flavors of raisin and chocolate layered atop this coffee's silky body.
 
Pronunciation: REE-oh day ah-BAY-hass

products.title: Kamavindi
products.body_html:
The words "inspired" and "passionate" only begin to describe the Mbature family, owners of the Kamavindi estate. With attention to every detail, they have implemented countless quality innovations that set their third-generation farm apart from others in the region. Their drive and dedication to quality are on display in this coffee, which strikes a lip smacking balance of juicy, blood orange-like acidity, syrupy sweetness and a nectarine finish.

Pronunciation: KAH-mah-VIN-dee

products.title: Finca Aurora – Anaerobic Java
products.body_html:
The Java variety has a long history, with its genetic origins traced to regional landraces in western Ethiopia. As a variety known for producing high quality, the team at Finca Aurora has experimented with anaerobic processing to further accentuate Java’s unique potential. When done well, coffees processed in this way often result in profiles that are more fruit-forward and vibrant than their traditionally-washed counterparts. This particular convergence of genetics and anaerobic processing produced one of the most unique coffees we've tasted from Nicaragua. In this small lot, we find flavors of dried apricot and honey, bolstered by a tea-like mouthfeel.

Pronunciation: FEEN-cuh AH-roar-ah JAH-va

products.title: Kabtamu Family – Natural Sundried
products.body_html:
The husband and wife team of Geremew Dambi and Tsehay Kabtamu work hand-in-hand to produce natural-sundried coffees with attention to detail that's evident in every cup. Geremew and Tsehay belong to the Jabanto farmers group, an organization that produces some of our favorite coffees in Yirgacheffe. When tasting this year’s offerings from Jabanto, the Kabtamu family’s lot stood out for its complex sweetness and acidity. In this classic Yirgacheffe profile, we find bright notes of fresh blueberry and citrus.

Geremew and Tsehay are pictured here on their family farm.

Pronunciation: kab-TAH-moo FAH-meh-lee

products.title: Decaf Urcunina
products.body_html:
A delicious cup of decaf coffee is a beautiful thing. This special lot was harvested by the Urcunina group in Nariño, Colombia, and decaffeinated at Colombia’s only decaffeination plant, using a sugarcane derivative called ethyl acetate to extract the caffeine. The result is one of the sweetest and most complex cups of decaf we've tasted, with notes of maple syrup, green grape, and a silky body. 

Pronunciation: DEE-caf ur-coo-NEE-nuh

products.title: Finca Santa Elena – Pacamara Variety
products.body_html:
Pacamara originated in El Salvador by crossbreeding the local Pacas variety with Maragogipe, a cultivar known for its large seeds and bold fruit flavors. This distinctive hybrid has become synonymous with high cup quality in the country and remains a staple of Salvadoran specialty coffee. When expertly cultivated and processed on the slopes of the Santa Ana volcano at Finca Santa Elena, it shines with crisp green apple brightness, balanced by milk chocolate and honey sweetness.


Pronunciation: pah-kah-MAH-rah

products.title: Juana Gaspar
products.body_html:
In the highlands of western Guatemala, near the town of Concepción Huista, Juana Gaspar’s small farm produces exceptional coffee emblematic of the entire region. Juana is a part of the CODECH cooperative, an organization we’ve worked with closely since 2010. Each season, the cooperative tastes each farmer's delivery, setting aside the highest-scoring lots to be sold at a premium, incentivizing and rewarding quality on a farm level. Juana’s coffee is regularly one of the top-scoring coffees each season. After hundreds of cups tasted, the coop once again identified this coffee as one of the best of the harvest, and our sourcing team couldn’t agree more. Enjoy densely sweet black cherry and plum notes balanced by crisp, well-structured acidity.


Pronunciation: WAH-nah Gahs-PAHR

products.title: Gundikhan Estate
products.body_html:
Gundikhan Estate, despite its modern approaches, feels historic. It is owned by passionate wildlife enthusiast Saif Ulla, who prioritizes harmony between humans and nature. Saif’s agricultural vision promotes biodiversity in an area exceptionally rich in species, including the neighboring Bhadra Tiger Reserve. The result is a feel-good coffee with sweet notes of tamarind, chocolate, and clove.

Pronunciation: GUN-dee-kahn Estate

Images Courtesy of David Stallings, Osito Coffee

products.title: Pablo Cordoba
products.body_html:
Pablo Cordoba is an exceptional farmer from Nariño, Colombia, who produces some of the best Colombian coffee we source each year. He has become a key partner in our Santafé sourcing, inspiring his neighbors to improve quality and coordinating the delivery of the community's coffee to our export partner, Toldopamba. These efforts have connected many in Santafé with the quality premiums Toldopamba offers for exceptional coffee. This year, Cordoba’s coffee tastes like a complex dark chocolate, layered with deep fruit tones akin to dried fig and black cherry.

Pronunciation: PAH-blo cor-DOE-ba

products.title: Finca Santa Elena
products.body_html:
Finca Santa Elena was nearly destroyed during the eruption of the Santa Ana volcano in 2005. For owner Fernando Lima, the disaster became a turning point. He rebuilt the farm with a focus on quality, replanting and adopting cultivation, processing, and drying practices that improved both sustainability and cup quality. Today, Finca Santa Elena stands as a testament to resilience and innovation, offering some of the best coffee in the region. We taste roasted cocoa, with a sweet cashew nuttiness and dried cherry finish. 

Pronunciation: FEEN-kah SAHN-tah ee-LAY-nah

products.title: Concepción Huista
products.body_html:
The towering mountains of western Guatemala are home to some of Central America's most interesting and high-quality coffees. This is undoubtedly true of coffee from the CODECH cooperative in the town of Concepción Huista. Between the high elevation, skilled processing, and rigorous quality control, these coffees pop with notes of cherry and apple and have a round, creamy body.

Pronunciation: con-SEP-see-ohn haw-WEE-sta

products.title: Cueva de los Llanos – Pink Bourbon Variety
products.body_html: The Andes Mountains split into three ranges in Nariño, Colombia, creating stunning landscapes situated at ideal elevations for coffee production. On a high ridge in the eastern range, members of the Agrounidos coffee association take advantage of their natural resources to produce some of the best coffees in the region. We work closely with the association every year to select the best lots for our menu. This small Pink Bourbon selection is the best of this harvest, offering distinct, vibrant acidity and notes of rose hips & pink lemonade.

products.title: Kabeywa – Natural Sundried
products.body_html:
Our partners at the Kawacom washing station stand on the forefront of specialty coffee production in Uganda, a country that primarily produces commercial-grade robustas. Using high-quality arabica grown in Mount Elgon’s fertile soil, Kawacom’s natural-sundried process prioritizes quality and consistency at every step. The resulting coffee redefines what we expect Ugandan coffee to taste like. Look for notes of concord grape, strawberry, and a cashew finish.

Pronunciation: Kah-bey-u-WAH

products.title: Finca El Puente
products.body_html:
We met Marysabel Caballero and Moisés Herrera, owners of Finca El Puente, in 2005. They have become like family to Counter Culture, and their constant pursuit of coffee perfection inspires us year after year. This year’s harvest has rich notes of nougat and cocoa, accented by an apricot acidity.

Pronunciation: FEEN-ka el PWEHN-teh

products.title: Blend Box Subscription
products.body_html:
Want to taste every Counter Culture blend and get free shipping while you do it? Now you can, with our Blend Box Subscription! Every two weeks, our Coffee Team selects two different blends for this subscription.

The coffees in rotation include Apollo, Big Trouble, Fast Forward, Forty-Six, Hologram, Gradient, and our seasonal blends.

Two 12 oz bags total with each shipment.

Your credit card will be billed per shipment. Subscriptions begin the business day after your order is placed.

products.title: Finca La Victoria
products.body_html:
Finca La Victoria sits nestled in the quiet pine forests of Dipilto, Nicaragua, a community widely known for producing some of the best coffees in the country. Year after year, the Lovo family works with their dedicated staff to improve coffee quality by refining their systems—from farm health to fermentation techniques. This year’s efforts have yielded a sweet and approachable coffee with notes of pecan, vanilla, and red apple. 

Pronunciation: FEEN-cuh lah vick-TOR-ee-uh

products.title: Idido
products.body_html:
The coffees we purchase from the Idido cooperative are simply remarkable. They’re among the highest-quality offerings we buy each year, and come from our longest-running partnership in East Africa. Idido’s members reside in some of Ethiopia's highest-elevation coffee-growing areas. This terroir is renowned for producing highly aromatic, complex coffee flavors. We taste delicate floral notes alongside flavors of melon and citrus.

Pronunciation: ee-DEE-doe

products.title: Office Coffee Subscription
products.body_html:
You’ve got a package waiting at the front desk: our new Office Subscription! These five-pound bags of whole-bean coffee are guaranteed to brighten the breakroom. Select your favorite whole-bean coffee and choose the delivery cadence that’s right for you.

Want us to decide for you? The Roaster's Choice selection changes every four weeks, ensuring no one gets bored with the office coffee.

products.title: Kabeywa
products.body_html:
The company behind this offering, Kawacom, continually sets new standards for the quality of Ugandan coffee year after year. Specially sourced from farms in Kabeywa, one of the highest-elevation communities on Mount Elgon, this coffee exemplifies excellence. The coffee underwent multiple washings under the supervision of Kawacom’s quality manager, Deus Nsubuga, to maximize the clarity of the cup. With flavors of stone fruit, citrus, chocolate, Kabeywa stands as a remarkable and forward-thinking representation of washed Ugandan coffee.

Pronunciation: Kah-bey-u-WAH

products.title: Makali – Subscriber Exclusive
products.body_html:
This coffee comes to us via Mountain Harvest, a company working to improve the quality of Ugandan coffee while making coffee communities more sustainable. We’ve been partners since 2018, their first season of production, noting and encouraging improvements over time. For the second year in a row, we are thrilled to offer Makali as a subscriber-exclusive product.

Forty-five women in the Makali community produced this coffee. Women in eastern Africa do much of the work to produce coffee, but are not often encouraged to participate in its trade. Mountain Harvest’s gender-equity training has helped transform these women’s ownership over their product. In addition, the organization’s technical assistance, microfinance program, and diversification projects positively impact the farmers and the quality of their coffee.

products.title: La Hierba Santa
products.body_html:
In the remote community of La Higuera, Jose Maria Campos and his family cultivate a unique coffee variety exhibiting a balance of excellent flavor, resilience, and high productivity. Our first visit to the farm left us with a sense that the coffee would be special. Time and again, Jose’s coffee stands out on the cupping table–confirming our impression after that first meeting. This lot bursts with juicy flavors of pomegranate and blood orange. 

Pronunciation: la he-ERR-ba SAN-ta

products.title: Finca Pashapa – Dark Roast
products.body_html:
Finca Pashapa, owned by the Salazar family in western Honduras, is our longest-standing coffee supplier. Their steadfast commitment to sustainable farm management, even in the face of significant climate challenges, has been inspiring to witness. This year, we're featuring their coffee as a dark-roasted, single-origin selection. Finca Pashapa Dark Roast features rich flavors of dark chocolate and roasted marshmallow with a velvety texture, embodying the depth of our collaboration.

Pronunciation: FEEN-cuh pah-SHOP-ah

products.title: Cueva de los Llanos
products.body_html: The Andes Mountains split into three ranges in Nariño, Colombia, creating a stunning landscape at ideal altitudes for coffee production. On a high ridge in the eastern range, members of the Agrounidos coffee association take advantage of their natural resources to produce some of the best coffees in the region. We work closely with the association every year to select the best lots for Cueva de los Llanos. Look for notes of green grape, almond, and milk chocolate.

products.title: Lucio Luque – Gesha Variety
products.body_html:
Located on the outskirts of Amaybamba—a small village deep within the Incahuasi Valley—is Lucio Luque’s young coffee parcel, Nuevo Progresso. This portion of his farm is unique in that it was planted with a single variety, which although was initially thought to be SL-09 was later discovered to be Gesha. His excitement and intentional planting of this variety piqued our attention, and we worked with the cooperative and our supply chain partners to isolate Lucio’s coffee from the larger blend it would have otherwise been destined for. The resulting coffee is delicately floral and reminiscent of bubble gum and grapefruit.

We're excited to offer a limited amount of this coffee in special 4oz packaging that includes a Jenna Gotthelf trading card, while supplies last. Jenna, our Wholesale Education Manager, used Lucio Luque's Gesha coffee in her run for the US Barista Championship.

products.title: Buliza Dark Roast
products.body_html:
The Buliza coffee washing station sits high in the hills of the Rulindo district, a short drive from Rwanda's  bustling capital of Kigali. Farmers belonging to the UCOCARU cooperative union bring their fresh coffee cherries to Buliza for processing, under the care of the washing station's experienced quality team. We’re once again sharing this lot as a dark-roasted single origin as a nod to our many customers who prefer this style of roasting. We taste deep notes of fig alongside syrupy notes of molasses and dark chocolate.

Pronunciation: boo-LEE-zuh

products.title: Nueva Llusta
products.body_html:
Members of the CENAPROC cooperative have long produced our favorite coffees from Bolivia. Over our 20+ year relationship, the organic coffees grown in the Yungas jungle of the country’s eastern mountains have consistently endured complicated logistical hurdles, making their quality all the more remarkable. This lot represents the best of these dedicated farmers, showcasing subtle cherry notes and a complex sweetness reminiscent of vanilla and hazelnut. 

Pronunciation: NWEH-vah USED-tuh

products.title: Buchiro – Natural Sundried
products.body_html:
A vast majority of natural-processed coffee from the Democratic Republic of the Congo is produced with haste, leading to poor quality coffee and low prices for producers. The Muungano cooperative, always seeking to push their potential, has honed their skills to prepare some of the highest quality natural-sundried lots from this often overlooked origin. Staff at the Buchiro washing station select strictly ripe coffee cherries and employ methodical drying techniques to produce a coffee with notes of berry, nougat, and cacao nibs.

 
Pronunciation: boo-CHEER-oh

products.title: Perennial
products.body_html:
For more than 30 years, Counter Culture has built lasting relationships with people who share our vision for quality and sustainability. These partnerships ensure that coffee can flourish for years to come. 

Perennial is a certified organic blend of coffees from some of our longest-standing producer relationships. With a full-bodied profile and rich notes of juicy fig and sweet dark chocolate, this coffee embodies the depth of the partnerships that make it possible.

products.title: Yacuanquer
products.body_html:
The town of Yacuanquer is relatively new to coffee production, but there’s nothing entry-level about their product. The area’s historically cool climate has recently changed to conditions suitable to grow specialty coffee. This coffee is produced by 19 farmers in Yacuanquer working with Toldopamba Coffee. The farmers’ dedication to quality coupled with Toldopamba’s technical assistance produces a delightful cup laden with sweet notes of pear and almond.

(Pronunciation: yah-kwan-CARE)

products.title: Damian Espinoza – Natural Sundried
products.body_html: We have purchased—and loved—Damian Espinoza’s coffee since 2018, and it’s been a staple on our menu each year. When we heard of Damian’s experiments with natural-sundried lots, our curiosity was piqued. This style of processing is uncommon in Peru. This lot is one of the cleanest examples of natural processing we’ve encountered from this region, brimming with flavors of Concord grape, creamsicle, and almond.

products.title: Damian Espinoza
products.body_html:
We were introduced to Damian Espinoza during our first year working with Origin Coffee Lab, a specialty exporter in Peru. Since then, we’ve purchased his coffee every year and had the privilege of visiting his farm in Chirinos numerous times. During those visits, Damian has been quiet and reserved, but his coffee clearly speaks for itself. After placing highly in the Cup of Excellence, he has continued to explore new varieties and processing techniques in pursuit of quality. 
This washed lot, however, exemplifies the consistent balance of fruit flavors and sweetness that have long made Damian’s coffees stand out on the cupping table. We taste notes of chocolate, cherry, and panela. 

Pronunciation: DAH-me-en es-pee-NO-za

products.title: Incahuasi
products.body_html:
Rooted in Inca heritage and shaped by the rugged Andean landscape that defines the coffee’s journey, the remote communities of Peru’s Incahuasi Valley are united by a shared commitment to quality. Coffee is grown at elevations of 1,600 to 2,400 meters and carefully processed through collective infrastructure. The resulting coffee delivers flavors reminiscent of golden raisin, almond, and caramel.

Pronunciation: een-cuh-WAH-see

products.title: Los Charapanos
products.body_html: The highlands surrounding the town of Zumba host a patchwork of small coffee farms that grow delicious  varieties like Caturra, Typica and Bourbon. In this area, locals take pride in calling themselves “Charapanos,” a regional nickname inspired by a local species of ant that they describe as hardworking and steadfast. Such work ethic is evident in the quality of this coffee, which offers notes of brown sugar, orange, and graham cracker.

products.title: Abel Salinas
products.body_html:
Abel Salinas is a first-generation coffee grower in Saraguro, southern Ecuador, and a key figure in the town’s rise as an origin of exceptional coffee. Alongside neighboring farmers who transitioned from cattle production to coffee cultivation, Abel planted the Typica Mejorado cultivar and began experimenting with innovative post-harvest processing methods. His efforts quickly earned recognition, including a historic first-place prize at Ecuador’s first Cup of Excellence competition. This coffee is brimming with fruit complexity—sweet nectarine and bright blood orange flavors give way to more tropical fruit tones as the cup cools. 

Pronunciation: AH-bell sal-EEN-ahs

products.title: Buchiro
products.body_html:
It’s rare to find a coffee of this caliber from the Democratic Republic of the Congo. Though the potential to produce such high-quality coffee exists throughout eastern Congo, the logistical challenges to bring these coffees to your cup are staggering. Located on the serene shores of Lake Kivu, this organic-certified lot comes from the Buchiro washing station, managed by the Muungano cooperative. Rich volcanic soils, old Bourbon varieties, and breathtaking elevations converge in this selection to bring vibrant flavors of kiwi, lime and black tea.

Pronunciation: boo-CHEER-oh

products.title: Nuevo Amanecer
products.body_html:
In 2012, Catholic Relief Services launched the Borderlands project to connect coffee growers in Nariño with the specialty market, offering farmers who had been divided by regional conflict a new path to prosperity through collaboration. Agrocafe El Tambo is one of the farmer associations that emerged from this effort. They chose to brand their coffee as Nuevo Amanecer, Spanish for “New Dawn,” as a nod to the paradigm shift. Each year, we reserve the highest-scoring coffees from the participating associations exclusively for our 2-bag Single Origin subscribers. This year, Nuevo Amanecer was a standout, with syrupy sweetness and complex interplay of pomegranate and red-grape tones. 

Pronunciation: New-wAY-VO Ah-mON-Es-Sare

products.title: Mpemba – Natural Sundried
products.body_html:
This exquisite natural-sundried lot from the Kazoza N’Ikawa cooperative in Mpemba, Burundi, is one of our most anticipated offerings each year. When the group began experimenting with natural processing in 2014, high-quality naturals were highly uncommon in Burundi. Today, the country is known for producing some of the best natural-sundried lots in the region, and Mpemba remains our favorite. Meticulous coffee cherry selection and processing lead to dynamic and fruity flavors of fig and strawberry, complemented by a bright acidity.
 
Pronunciation: PEM-bah

products.title: Mpemba
products.body_html:
The village of Mpemba, a tiny and tranquil hamlet tucked into the rolling hills of Burundi’s Kayanza province, is home to the Kazoza N’Ikawa cooperative. In the Kirundi language, Kazoza N’Ikawa translates to “the future is coffee”—a name hinting at the commitment to quality exemplified by its members. The coffees we buy from the co-op are not only our favorites from Burundi but across the entire region. This washed lot exhibits all of the hallmarks that make Burundian coffees so unique. Look for juicy top notes of clementine intermingled with flavors of honey and a tea-like body.

Pronunciation: PEM-bah

products.title: Urcunina
products.body_html: The best coffees are not just about taste, they are examples of empowerment and camaraderie. By uniting forces in the ASPROCAES association and building this supply chain alongside Counter Culture, the producers of Urcunina transformed their production process and strengthened their resilience as a community. The coffee is classic Nariño: dried fruit notes complement a sweet caramel and chocolate base.

featured_image.alt: A 12 oz bag of Urcunina coffee from Narińo, Colombia.

products.title: Decaf K’uychi
products.body_html:
A delicious cup of decaf is a beautiful thing. This lot was harvested by the producers of K’uychi in Nariño, Colombia, and decaffeinated at Colombia’s only decaffeination plant, which uses a derivative of sugarcane, called ethyl acetate, in the process. The result is one of the sweetest and most complex cups of decaf we've ever tasted, with notes of black cherry, dried date, and molasses.

Pronunciation: Kew-wEE-Chi

products.title: Slow Motion – Decaf
products.body_html:
Slow down and savor a cup of coffee, simply because it’s delicious. We pay extra attention to our decaf coffee because you deserve a flavorful, full-bodied cup without the caffeine kick. With notes of molasses and cocoa, Slow Motion is equally delicious as any of our caffeinated coffees.

Decaffeination: Swiss Water Process unless otherwise noted.

products.title: Forty-Six
products.body_html: Forty-Six isn’t your average dark-roast coffee. Sourced from some of the world's most renowned coffee-growing regions, this extraordinary blend of organic-certified coffees is carefully chosen to maximize sweetness and maintain complexity through dark roasting. Forty-Six boasts a full-bodied profile where dark chocolate sweetness meets a smoky, roast-forward intensity.

products.title: Hologram
products.body_html: Elevate your coffee experience to a new dimension. Hologram is an extraordinary medium-roast blend that showcases the finest coffees from around the world. Tantalizing notes of ripe fruit and chocolate create a multidimensional flavor experience that’s as complex as it is approachable.

products.title: La Golondrina
products.body_html:
La Golondrina is a testament to the power of partnership. The Orgánica cooperative, unwavering in its commitment to sustainability, has produced our La Golondrina offering since 2007. This coffee has captured the hearts of our customers and has become our most popular single-origin offering. La Golondrina showcases quintessential Colombian coffee flavors, featuring a harmonious balance of zesty cherry, rich milk chocolate, and delightful nutty notes.

Pronunciation:  Lah go-lun-DREE-nuh

products.title: Gradient
products.body_html: Each sip of Gradient takes you on a journey through Colombia's coffee landscape. These high-quality Colombian coffees maintain their unique characteristics in this dark roast, resulting in a full-bodied and approachably sweet cup of coffee. With notes of dark chocolate, roasted nuts, and berries, Gradient is the perfect choice for coffee lovers who appreciate a dense and complex brew with a vibrant acidity.

products.title: Apollo
products.body_html: Experience the magic of Ethiopian coffee in every cup. Apollo is a year-round celebration of the delightful floral and citrus notes that Ethiopian coffees are renowned for. This special blend is thoughtfully roasted to showcase the coffee’s true flavors and honor Ethiopia's historical contribution of coffee to the global culture.

products.title: Big Trouble
products.body_html: For a coffee called Big Trouble, this blend delivers nutty, caramel, and chocolate flavors that are easy to love. Sourced from sustainable producers across the globe, this medium-dark roast blend is expertly roasted to ensure a consistently exceptional brew every time. Striking the ideal balance between sweet flavors and a satisfying medium body, it’s no wonder Big Trouble is our best-selling blend.
